test_banner.title: Karo is a test application
test_banner.intro: You are using a test version of Karo, used to validate features before the public launch. Data you enter may be reset or deleted at any time: we recommend using fictitious data rather than real financial information.
test_banner.no_payment: No real payment is made. You can choose a paid plan (Pro or Family) when signing up or with the buttons in the Pricing section: it is activated immediately, no card is charged, and you can try every feature of the chosen plan.
test_banner.accounts_desc: Add your bank accounts, credit cards and other debts. For a card, Karo tracks the balance, the credit limit and the utilization rate.
test_banner.envelopes_desc: Split each account's money into envelopes (rent, groceries, savings, etc.). Deposit, transfer or withdraw money, and pay a bill or a card directly from an envelope.
test_banner.paychecks_desc: Record your jobs and paychecks. Karo calculates how much of each paycheck goes into each envelope, based on your bills and their frequency. Fixed paychecks can also be created automatically.
test_banner.bills_desc: Keep your recurring bills and their payment frequency. The notification bell warns you about overdue bills, bills due within the next 7 days and suspended paychecks.
test_banner.sharing_desc: Invite family members by email and share common expenses within a household.
test_banner.planning_desc: A calendar shows upcoming bills and paychecks and projects the end-of-month balance. A chart shows how your account balances change over time.
test_banner.reports_desc: Review your spending statistics and how your budget evolves.
test_banner.privacy_desc: Your data is protected and you can export it. The interface is available in French and English.
test_banner.plans_title: Free or paid: what's the difference?
test_banner.plans_intro: The free plan is enough to discover Karo with a single account. Paid plans add more accounts and envelopes, family sharing and advanced analytics. During the test phase, they are activated without payment.
test_banner.free_6: No planning, balance history or advanced analytics
test_banner.plans_footnote: Default limits at the time of writing; the Karo team may change them.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: How Karo works, in a few answers.

envelope.question: What is an envelope?
envelope.answer: An envelope sets money aside for one purpose, like rent, groceries or a savings goal. Its balance is part of the account it is attached to.

accountVsEnvelope.question: What is the difference between an account and an envelope?
accountVsEnvelope.answer: The account holds the actual money. Envelopes split that balance between your planned uses. Surplus: the account balance is higher than the total of its envelopes. Deficit: the envelopes add up to more than the account balance.

expectedIncome.question: What does "Expected income / month" mean?
expectedIncome.answer: For each pay plan, we take the amount of the last paycheck received and multiply it by how many paychecks come in a month (weekly, every two weeks, twice a month, monthly, yearly). Irregular or one-time income counts as 0.

addIncome.question: How do I add an income?
addIncome.answer: Add an income from the dashboard. Enter its name, pay frequency and the account it is deposited into. You can make it your main income.

allocation.question: How do I split my pay across envelopes?
allocation.answer: When you create an envelope, choose a pay plan and an allocation type: bill (a share of the bill each paycheck), automatic withdrawal, fixed amount per paycheck, or percentage of the paycheck.

paid.question: What happens when I click "Paid"?
paid.answer: For a bill, the amount paid is withdrawn from the envelope and from the account balance, and the payment date is recorded. For a debt, the amount is withdrawn from the envelope and reduces what you owe on the debt account.

transferWithdraw.question: What is the difference between Transfer and Withdraw?
transferWithdraw.answer: Transfer moves money from one envelope to another in the same currency. Withdraw takes money out of the envelope without changing the account balance; tick "unexpected expense" for an expense you did not plan.

debt.question: Why can I not withdraw from a debt envelope?
debt.answer: A debt envelope is only used to repay the debt. Use "Pay the debt" to repay it.

sharing.question: How do I share an envelope with my household?
sharing.answer: Turn on the "shareable" option on the envelope. Other household members can then see it and link it to their own envelope.
